audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 3 draft aligned to Samuel's nighttime call and oracle concerning Eli's house; later source/witness audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: The boy Samuel was ministering to YHWH before Eli. Word of YHWH was rare in those days; vision was not breaking through.

familiar.text: And the child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli. And the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision.

verses.restored: It happened in that day that Eli was lying in his place. His eyes had begun to grow dim; he was not able to see.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at that time, when Eli was laid down in his place, and his eyes began to wax dim, that he could not see;

verses.restored: Lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying in temple of YHWH where ark of God was.

familiar.text: And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep;

verses.restored: YHWH called Samuel, and he said, Here I am.

familiar.text: That the LORD called Samuel: and he answered, Here am I.

verses.restored: He ran to Eli and said, Here I am, for you called me. He said, I did not call; return, lie down. So he went and lay down.

familiar.text: And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down.

verses.restored: YHWH again called, Samuel! Samuel arose, went to Eli, and said, Here I am, for you called me. He said, I did not call, my son; return, lie down.

familiar.text: And the LORD called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again.

verses.restored: Now Samuel did not yet know YHWH, and word of YHWH had not yet been revealed to him.

familiar.text: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, neither was the word of the LORD yet revealed unto him.

verses.restored: YHWH called Samuel again, third time. He arose, went to Eli, and said, Here I am, for you called me. Then Eli understood that YHWH was calling the boy.

familiar.text: And the LORD called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the LORD had called the child.

verses.restored: Eli said to Samuel, Go, lie down. If he calls you, say, Speak, YHWH, for your servant is listening. Samuel went and lay down in his place.

familiar.text: Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

verses.restored: YHWH came, stood, and called as time after time, Samuel! Samuel! Samuel said, Speak, for your servant is listening.

familiar.text: And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Samuel, Look, I am doing a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone hearing it will tingle.

familiar.text: And the LORD said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.

verses.restored: In that day I will establish against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, beginning and completing.

familiar.text: In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end.

verses.restored: I have told him that I am judging his house perpetually for the iniquity he knew: his sons were bringing contempt upon themselves, and he did not restrain them.

familiar.text: For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.

verses.restored: Therefore I have sworn to house of Eli: iniquity of house of Eli shall not be covered by sacrifice or offering perpetually.

familiar.text: And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.

verses.restored: Samuel lay until morning, then opened doors of house of YHWH. Samuel feared to tell the vision to Eli.

familiar.text: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision.

verses.restored: Eli called Samuel and said, Samuel, my son. He said, Here I am.

familiar.text: Then Eli called Samuel, and said, Samuel, my son. And he answered, Here am I.

verses.restored: He said, What is word that he spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. Thus may God do to you and thus add if you hide from me a word from all word that he spoke to you.

familiar.text: And he said, What is the thing that the LORD hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee.

verses.restored: Samuel told him all words and hid nothing from him. Eli said, He is YHWH; what is good in his eyes, let him do.

familiar.text: And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.

verses.restored: Samuel grew, and YHWH was with him and let none of his words fall to ground.

familiar.text: And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.

verses.restored: All Israel, from Dan to Beer-sheba, knew that Samuel was established as prophet to YHWH.

familiar.text: And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD.

verses.restored: YHWH continued to appear in Shiloh, for YHWH revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by word of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the LORD appeared again in Shiloh: for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

translation_notes: Samuel is a child serving within a compromised institution. His calling must not be used to normalize child labor, spiritual grooming, sleep disruption, or placing children near known abusers.
Eli's dim eyes are an age-related disability. Blindness or low vision is not spiritual dullness, moral failure, or punishment.
Samuel's repeated misrecognition is normal inexperience. Discernment grows through repetition and guidance rather than instant certainty.
Eli eventually helps Samuel recognize the call, showing that a compromised leader may still offer a true instruction; this does not erase his failures.
The narrative says YHWH stood and called. Mystical interpretation must remain distinct from source translation and cannot prescribe auditory experiences as universal proof of calling.
The message given to Samuel concerns adult institutional failure. Children should not be made responsible for investigating, announcing, or repairing leaders' abuse.
Eli pressures Samuel with an oath formula to disclose the vision. This power-laden demand should not become a model for forcing children to reveal private spiritual or traumatic material.
Verse 13 has a textual issue around the sons bringing a curse upon themselves versus cursing God; later witness audit is required.
Sacrifice cannot cover unaddressed abuse. Ritual, donation, confession, reputation, and office do not replace accountability and repair.
Eli's acceptance of judgment is not the same as repentance, survivor care, or structural reform.
'None of his words fell to the ground' marks recognized prophetic reliability, not personal infallibility in every opinion.
Dan to Beer-sheba is a territorial merism and must not be deployed to erase other peoples or modern political complexities.
safety_note: Do not use Samuel's call to groom children for religious labor, demand unquestioning obedience, pressure minors to disclose spiritual experiences, or burden them with adult institutional failures. Do not equate blindness with spiritual failure. Ritual cannot erase abuse; leadership accountability and survivor protection remain essential.
